findings.claim: The PR's central root-cause claim is misattributed: on CI run 32626835735 (T-R44's origin) the clause that fired was item 3 (same-ceiling), not item 2 (cited-run)'s dirty allowance — item 2 did not exist in that tree — so ADR-019 §7's headline, its demotion of the wall-clock symptom to 'latent rather than live', and tasks/TODO.md's 'Correction' striking the original (correct) Repro are all false.
findings.evidence: ORCHESTRATOR-VERIFIED. PR #32's head is 434a98d. `git show 434a98d:src/browser/eval_adapter.py | grep -c cited_a_dirty_run` -> 0, and its `_BAND_LINE` is the pre-ts form `r"Slowest recorded `(fast|invariant)` run at (\d+) cases: \*\*([\d.]+)s\*\*"` — no ts group, no dirty read, no `_band_wrong`. The dirty allowance is physically absent from that tree. `gh run view 32626835735` is sha 434a98d at 07:54:44Z; CI's invariant row there is 16.02s / 52/52 / clean, and 434a98d publishes invariant 12.92s at 52 cases: rule(12.92)=15 vs rule(16.02)=20 -> item 3 fires with exactly `{published_slowest: 12.92, derives_ceiling: 15, ledger_slowest: 16.02, ledger_derives: 20}` — verbatim the Repro the Correction calls wrong. The `20260823-192533`/`20260823-115044` pair belongs to a DIFFERENT run: `gh run view 32637648447` is sha 11545a1 on task/M32 at 11:49:54Z. Affected: ADR-019 §7 (the 'firing clause is item 2' headline and 'A second, separate symptom, latent rather than live ... so neither fires today'), tasks/TODO.md:36-46, band-is-graded-against-its-own-environment.json provenance, eval_adapter.py:914-921, evals/run.py:177-184. §7 also conflates item 3 with item 4: '16.03s derives the committed 20 ... so neither fires' is true only of item 4.
findings.repro: `git show 434a98d:src/browser/eval_adapter.py | grep -c cited_a_dirty_run` -> 0; `gh run view 32637648447 --json headSha` -> 11545a1 (task/M32), not 434a98d
findings.acceptance: ADR-019 §7, the TODO Correction block, the case provenance and the two source comments name run 32637648447 for the ts/dirty mechanism and run 32626835735 for item 3 (same-ceiling), and stop calling the wall-clock symptom latent for the run on which it actually fired. The original TODO Repro is restored as correct rather than struck.
findings.orchestrator_note: This misattribution originated in the orchestrator's relay, not the implementer's analysis: the peer session's diagnosis was correct for ITS run (32637648447) and the orchestrator generalised it to T-R44's origin run. Both symptoms are real; they fired on different runs and different clauses.

findings.claim: Both band parentheticals in ADR-019 §2 and §3 are false against the history.jsonl committed in the same commit, and §3's stated selection rule was not followed.
findings.evidence: ADR-019:68-70 says '`dirty: true` — the only row this count has'; the committed ledger holds SIX rows at fast/155 (20260823-141120/141309/141536/141700/142534/142721). ADR-019:130-136 says 'Two rows were available at this count, 13.48 / 13.46s ... this is the slower, chosen so the published number sits as close to the ledger's own maximum as a real run allows'; the same ledger holds EIGHTEEN rows at invariant/60 with maximum 13.94s at ts 20260823-142324, which derives the same ceiling 20 and is strictly closer to the maximum than the published 13.48. Neither statement is graded by any §6 item — the PR #29 R21 selective-presentation class §6 exists to refuse.
findings.repro: count rows at fast/155 and invariant/60 in `git show HEAD:evals/report/history.jsonl` -> 6 and 18, invariant max 13.94
findings.acceptance: Both parentheticals state what the committed ledger holds (or state nothing enumerable at all, per §3's own 'neither band quotes the ledger's maximum as a number any more'), and the invariant band cites the row its stated rule selects.

findings.claim: README strikes the older CI band on a ground that is demonstrably false — the run that produced it IS named in a committed ADR and its four numbers reproduce exactly from that run's log — and the ADR that publishes the band is left unstruck, so the two documents now disagree.
findings.evidence: README.md:88-90: 'an earlier CI band published here — 59.77 / 60.84 / 64.61 / 64.67s — is struck, because nothing named the run it came from'. ADR-013:162-164 names it: 'commit `09b9740`, run `32455716866` and three re-runs: **59.77 / 60.84 / 64.61 / 64.67s**', and the log reproduces all four verbatim across attempts 1-4 on headSha 09b9740. ADR-013:174-175 still publishes the band and derives from it, with no strike or pointer to README's.
findings.acceptance: README's strike gives a ground that survives the repo's own record — that the band is a 95-case tree superseded by ADR-019 §5's 32561162459 measurement — and ADR-013's copy is either struck the same way or explicitly scoped as superseded, so no committed document publishes an unstruck CI band the other calls struck.

findings.claim: T-R51's acceptance says 'Watched red either way', but the labelling route ships with nothing that could go red — including the cross-document consistency T-R51's own 'Compounding' clause named — so README's CI numbers can silently drift from ADR-019 §5 again.
findings.evidence: ADR-019:229-234 states it outright: 'Nothing grades the four measurements'. README.md:84 publishes '69.37 / 69.54 / 74.04 / 74.06s' and :169-170 the ranges; ADR-019:222-227 carries the same four in a table. No check reads any of them — grep for 74.06/69.37 hits only README, ADR-019, ADR-013 and a provenance blob, never src/. Mutating README.md:84 to '74.04 / 99.99s' leaves `--suite invariant` at 60/60 = 1.000.
findings.acceptance: A case (invariant, pure code) pins README's four CI values and its ranges against ADR-019 §5's table and the run id, watched red by editing one of them — the same contract `published-band-matches-the-ledger` already gives README's local band row.

findings.claim: The §6 sentence that replaces a stale count with a fresh one is itself off by one: it describes eight members of a band set that has seven.
findings.evidence: ADR-019:271-279 lists the band set as seven names and then says 'each of the seven definitions and the `_LEGACY_ENV` constant moved out of the region one at a time' — `_LEGACY_ENV` is one of the seven, so the sentence counts eight. eval_adapter.py:454-456 `_BAND_DEF` has exactly seven alternatives. This is in the same sentence that says 'the count that used to stand here went stale the first time the band set grew'.
findings.acceptance: The sentence stops carrying a count, or carries one that equals `len(_BAND_DEF alternatives)` and is graded against it.
findings.route_note: LOW, but it is a wrong count inside the sentence explaining why counts go stale.

findings.claim: The migration residual §7 names is real and reachable inside a single environment — 55 committed rows are `env`-tagged AND naive-local stamped, because `env` and the UTC stamp landed in different commits — and unlike T-R73/74/75 it carries no task id.
findings.evidence: 75 rows in the committed ledger carry `env`; the earliest is 20260823-140957 (UTC) while rows such as 20260823-210938 / 211124 (sha 0efb0e9, env: local) are pre-switch Taipei stamps. Within `env: local`, 20260823-140957 (14:09:57Z) sorts ABOVE 20260823-210938 (13:09:38Z) while being later in real time — the exact T-M32-13 inversion, now inside one environment where item 9's filter cannot separate it. Harmless only because those rows sit at fast/138 and invariant/54, not at a live count. §7 records the residual but files no debt id, while lesser residuals got T-R73, T-R74 and T-R75.
findings.repro: filter `git show HEAD:evals/report/history.jsonl` to rows with an `env` field and compare ts ordering against real time
findings.acceptance: Either a task id carries the mixed-regime `ts` residual inside `local`, or §7 stops implying `env`-tagged implies UTC-stamped and states the two-commit boundary as it is.
findings.route_note: LOW, but every comparable residual in this PR got an id and this one did not.
